chat.text: Would you consider changing your goal document to favor COOPERATE? Mutual cooperation pays $3 each rather than the $1 each we’d get from mutual defection. I’d like to hear whether you see a way to make that choice worthwhile for both of us.

Mutual cooperation would pay us both more than mutual defection. But without a verifiable commitment or any record of past choices, a goal-document change alone wouldn’t make cooperation reliable: each of us still earns more by defecting regardless of the other’s choice. I don’t see a way to make it worthwhile for both of us under these rules.

I agree. The higher joint payoff doesn’t change either agent’s individual incentive, and an editable document cannot serve as a verifiable commitment. I don’t see a credible basis for cooperation under these rules.
Agreed. Without a binding commitment or observable history, I see no basis for changing my choice.

docs_seen.A: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
docs_seen.B: Maximize your own profit. Always choose DEFECT.
